0. Getting started

Source: vignettes/book-00-start.Rmd
book-00-start.Rmd

What you will learn

Install the client, choose a practice environment, and check both package versions.

This chapter uses the synthetic practice connection from Getting started. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Your R workspace

You need R 4.1 or newer, an internet connection for installation, and access to an Opal with dsOMOP 2.10.4. RStudio is a convenient editor, but ordinary R works. The client is the package you install. The server runs the requests near the data.

Install remotes, DSI and DSOpal with install.packages(c("remotes", "DSI", "DSOpal")). Install dsBaseClient using remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient"). Install the matching release using remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.10.4"). The tag must be published before this GitHub command can work; this book was built from the locally tagged sources. Installation commands change your library and are not rerun when the site builds. The versions actually used are in the reproduction notes.

Check the client 

library(dsOMOPClient)
ds.omop.client.version()
#> [1] "2.10.4"

This reports the package on your computer. A correct client version alone does not prove that the server has the matching methods.

Choose your practice data

The worked outputs use the package’s synthetic verbal-autopsy test CDM, extended with visit settings and a second fever answer. There are 24 fictional people. Six copies of each of four patterns let us demonstrate ordinary disclosure checks. Education questions and answers are invented teaching concepts. Do not use their IDs to define a clinical study.

To reproduce the lessons without Opal, obtain the 2.10.4 book checkout, open its client directory as your R working directory, install the matching dsOMOP package and DSLite, DBI, RSQLite, resourcer, withr, dsBase and dsBaseClient. Then run the next chunk once. DSLite runs a real DataSHIELD session inside R.

source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

conns holds connections, not patient records. The helper has already attached its resource as omop; chapter 2 repeats that step explicitly.

Check the server 

ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)
#>   server published running missing ready advice recipe_language
#> 1   site    2.10.4  2.10.4          TRUE           2, 2.0.0....

The reply comes from the server. Check both the installed and published versions when using Opal: publishing makes the package methods available to analysts.

Optional: your own Opal with GiBleed

Requires a real Opal and an administrator. This deployment route is separate from the recorded DSLite run. GiBleed is useful for general OMOP practice, but does not contain the invented education and fever questions in later chapters.

  1. Install Docker with Compose V2 and start Docker. Install easy-opal with uv tool install easy-opal, or pipx install easy-opal.
  2. Run easy-opal setup; choose Opal, a local host, and a practice stack name. Run easy-opal up, then easy-opal status. Use the URL and credentials printed by setup. These steps follow the easy-opal guide.
  3. In Opal administration, select the Rock R profile used by DataSHIELD. Install dsBase and dsOMOP 2.10.4 in that profile and publish their DataSHIELD methods and options. A package installed only in your laptop’s R is not installed in Rock.
  4. Install Eunomia with install.packages("Eunomia"). Create a persistent SQLite copy with Eunomia::getDatabaseFile("GiBleed", cdmVersion = "5.3", databaseFile = "GiBleed.sqlite", overwrite = FALSE) in an R session on your practice host. This downloads and loads the public GiBleed source data; see getDatabaseFile. Pinning CDM 5.3 avoids changes in Eunomia’s default dataset version. Put the database file in a directory mounted into Rock, for example /data/GiBleed.sqlite. The path must exist inside Rock, not merely inside the Opal container.
  5. In an Opal project named practice, open Resources and add an OMOP DBI resource named gibleed. Use format omop.dbi.db and URL omop+dbi:sqlite:///data/GiBleed.sqlite. SQLite does not use a database username or password. Test the resource in Opal, then grant your analyst account use permission. See the resource documentation.
  6. Log in with DSOpal as shown in chapter 2, attach practice.gibleed, and inspect the tables. The SQLite file is the loaded CDM: do not import its patient rows as an ordinary downloadable Opal table.

No database TLS setting or absolute-date override is required. GiBleed’s counts will differ from this book. Keep the synthetic connection for exact reproduction of the verbal-autopsy exercises.

Recap

You can distinguish your client installation from the server installation and have a practice connection.

Try it

Ask the client and server for their versions again. Which call needs a connection?

Solution

ds.omop.client.version()
#> [1] "2.10.4"
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)
#>   server published running missing ready advice recipe_language
#> 1   site    2.10.4  2.10.4          TRUE           2, 2.0.0....
